1.diagnosis: This is the first experiment in the AUTORESEARCHTABULAR campaign on the Higgs UCI benchmark (Baldi 2014, frozen 10M / 500k / 500k split). No prior experimental evidence exists yet, so the immediate goal is to anchor the leaderboard at a defensible lightgbm baseline using registry-default hyperparameters per the primary paper. Without a baseline anchor, all later capacity, regularisation, and seed-variance probes are uninterpretable. The first run also confirms that the audit gate fingerprint, composite-formula fingerprint, and reasoning gate all interlock correctly end-to-end.
1.citations: Ke, Meng, Finley, Wang, Chen, Ma, Ye, Liu 2017 NeurIPS 'LightGBM: A Highly Efficient Gradient Boosting Decision Tree' (arXiv:1711.08251) — leaf-wise tree growth with histogram bins, GOSS (Gradient-based One-Side Sampling) and EFB (Exclusive Feature Bundling). The published Higgs UCI experiments in section 4 establish LightGBM as the fastest GBM framework on multi-million-row datasets and the natural starting point for tabular gradient-boosting on the Baldi 2014 frozen split.
1.hypothesis: Recipe 'default 1000 leaves 63 lr 0.05' for lightgbm: registry default per Ke 2017 §4 Higgs experiment. We hypothesise that this hyperparameter change will move the validation AUROC by a measurable but bounded delta vs the within-backbone running mean — typically in the 0.001-0.020 range on Higgs depending on which axis is being probed. Direction (positive vs negative delta) is governed by the published recommendation in the primary citation: capacity-up moves help when the model is underfit, regularisation-up moves help when it is overfit, and seed-variance moves serve only to bound noise rather than to chase mean. The val/test gap should stay within 0.005 because the Baldi 2014 split is large (500k each) and Higgs is i.i.d. by construction; gaps wider than that flag implementation bugs rather than genuine model behaviour.
1.prediction: Predict val AUROC and test AUROC each in the published lightgbm-on-Higgs range with val/test gap ≤ 0.005. Composite expected within 0.02 of the published baseline. Failure mode: composite < 0.50 indicates implementation bug or label flip and triggers an audit re-run before continuing.
1.verdict: Experiment #1 (lightgbm: exp1 [lightgbm#1] default 1000 leaves 63 lr 0.05) finished in 96.7s with status KEEP/CHAMPION. Composite 0.8301 (val_auc 0.8305, test_auc 0.8302, train_auc 0.8504). Val/test gap 0.0004 — within tolerance band of 0.005 expected on Baldi 2014 frozen split. Calibration ECE val 0.0126 test 0.0117. The composite-fingerprinted formula and split-fingerprint gate both held. Result is deterministic given the recorded seed and recipe; rerunning under the same seed must reproduce the metrics within float-eps.
1.learning: This lightgbm experiment slots into the campaign at composite 0.8301. Compared to the running within-backbone best, the move is the new champion. For the next recipe in the lightgbm arc, the campaign script will probe a different hyperparameter axis — capacity, regularisation, or seed-variance — based on the post-run delta vs prediction. If val_auc and test_auc moved together (gap < 0.005), generalisation is healthy and we can push capacity; if val gained but test lost, the move overfit and the next experiment must regularise. Knowledge gained: the (backbone, axis-direction) pair has been bound to a quantitative composite delta for cross-backbone comparison once all 25 recipes complete.
